name: Budgeting
blurb: The plan for the money you already earn, before it disappears.
intro: Budgets get sold as restriction. They work better as permission: this much for rent, this much for saving, this much to spend without checking the balance first. Everything in this category is the version that survives a real first salary.
seoTitle: Budgeting Posts for Your First Salary
meta: Budgeting guides for your first salary: how to split a paycheck, automate savings and keep a life you actually enjoy. No shame, no spreadsheets you'll abandon.

name: Saving
blurb: Building a cushion so a bad week doesn't become a bad year.
intro: Saving on an entry-level salary is not about willpower, it is about removing the decision. These posts are about the cushion: what to build, how much, and what to do when the numbers feel too small to matter.
meta: Realistic saving guides for entry-level salaries: how to build an emergency fund, automate transfers and keep going when rent eats half your paycheck.

name: Mistakes
blurb: The expensive lessons someone else already paid for.
intro: Nobody hands you a manual for the first year of real money, so most people learn by paying for it. This category is the shortcuts: the mistakes that cost the most, why they happen, and the small fix that undoes most of the damage.
seoTitle: Money Mistakes to Skip in Your Twenties
meta: The money mistakes new grads make most often, what each one costs over a year, and the simple fix for each. Learn them from someone else's receipts.

name: Career
blurb: The job hunt, the offer and the money behind both.
intro: Your salary is the biggest number in your budget, so the job is part of the money conversation. This is the shelf for getting hired, reading an offer properly and making the next move count.
meta: Honest career advice for people in their first job: what changed in hiring, the job posts to avoid, and what actually gets you an offer.
